de-nonnative-reptile-permit.title: Delaware Code, Title 3, Chapter 72 — Possession of Mammals or Reptiles Exotic to Delaware
de-nonnative-reptile-permit.note: §7201 requires a permit before bringing in, possessing, selling, or exhibiting any live wild mammal or reptile not native to Delaware; the California kingsnake, a Pacific coast species, falls under this permit requirement.

md-not-native.title: Md. Code, Criminal Law § 10-621, Import, Offer, or Transfer of Dangerous Animal
md-not-native.note: The dangerous-animal list covers only specific mammals, crocodilians, and venomous snakes of four named families; non-venomous colubrids like the kingsnake and companion birds like cockatoos are both absent from it.

al-exotic-birds.title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 220-2-.26, Restrictions On Possession, Sale, Importation And/Or Release Of Certain Animals And Fish
al-exotic-birds.note: Same rule already sourced for other species' prohibited list; its bans reach only federally-listed Lacey Act injurious wildlife and named out-of-state mammal/fish species, with no bird species named, so a captive-bred parrot or cockatoo falls outside it.

az-exotic-birds.title: Arizona Revised Statutes § 17-306, Importation, Transportation, Release or Possession of Live Wildlife
az-exotic-birds.note: General prohibition on unauthorized live wildlife; enforced in practice through the companion restricted-species rule (R12-4-406), which is aimed at native and dangerous wildlife and does not name common psittacine pets.

de-birds-exempt.title: Delaware Code, Title 3, Chapter 72 — Possession of Mammals or Reptiles Exotic to Delaware
de-birds-exempt.note: The permit requirement in §7201 names only wild mammals and non-native reptiles; birds are absent from the chapter's operative text despite appearing in its older title reference, so a pet cockatoo needs no permit under this chapter.

ne-cage-aviary-birds.title: 163 Neb. Admin. Code, ch. 4, § 008 — Keeping Wildlife in Captivity (Definitions)
ne-cage-aviary-birds.note: Same chapter as ne-163-nac-4-008; its opening definitions section defines 'Cage and Aviary Birds' verbatim as captive-reared, non-native birds such as parrots, exotic finches, and canaries, with the monk parakeet the one species carved back out.

nv-unprotected-birds.title: Nevada Administrative Code § 503.110, Restrictions on Importation, Transportation and Possession of Certain Species
nv-unprotected-birds.note: The prohibited-species list under this section names only three birds (Pink Starling/Rosy Pastor, Red-billed Dioch, Red-whiskered Bulbul); cockatoos and other companion parrots are absent.
